entries.title: The Chicago Marathon is this weekend. Here’s why it’s distinctive and attracts runners
entries.summary: <p>The Chicago Marathon is a glorious and festive fall event for many, especially the estimated 1.7 million spectators who don’t have to break a sweat. </p><p>For others running, the 26.2-mile course, can be grueling and painful.</p><p>The 48th running of the Chicago Marathon kicks off this year on Sunday at 7:20 a.m. It starts and finishes in Grant Park.</p><p>Information for participants and spectators, including schedules and logistics, can be found at <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicagomarathon.com/about/" target="_blank" ><u>ChicagoMarathon.com</u></a>, <a class="Link" href="https://www.choosechicago.com/articles/sports-and-recreation/the-chicago-marathon/" target="_blank" ><u>Choose Chicago</u></a>, the city’s tourism agency and the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/2026/10/06/2026-chicago-marathon-what-to-know-how-to-watch" target="_blank" ><u>Sun-Times</u></a>.</p><p>Many things make the marathon distinctive, as well as one of the biggest events on Chicago’s tourism calendar, according to Choose Chicago.</p><p>Here are some highlights:</p><h3>How many people will participate this year?</h3><p>More than 55,000 participants are expected for this year’s race, say <a class="Link" href="https://cdn.chicagomarathon.com/app/uploads/2026/09/22085346/092226_2026-BACM_Press-Release_Event-Updates.pdf" target="_blank" ><u>organizers</u></a>, who expect it to be the <a class="Link" href="https://newsroom.bankofamerica.com/content/newsroom/press-releases/2026/08/largest-bank-of-america-chicago-marathon-field-yet-fueled-by-ins.html" target="_blank" ><u>largest field</u></a> ever. Over 200,000 applied to join the 2026 race.</p><p>The Bank of America Chicago Marathon continues to grow. Last year, it drew 55,744 participants, a 4% increase from 2024. In 2023, it counted 48,472 finishers and 45,932 in 2019. The 2020 race was not held due to the COVID-19 pandemic.</p><p>The Chicago marathon is the fourth largest in the world in terms of finishers, based on races from 2024 to 2026, according to <a class="Link" href="https://marathonhandbook.com/biggest-marathons-in-the-world/" target="_blank" ><u>Marathon Handbook</u></a>. The top five are London (59,830 finishers), New York City (59,226), Paris (55,499), Chicago (54,351) and Berlin (54,280).</p><h3>Why is the course appealing to runners?</h3><p>The marathon is a scenic tour through 29 of Chicago’s <a class="Link" href="https://www.choosechicago.com/articles/sports-and-recreation/the-chicago-marathon/" target="_blank" ><u>77 neighborhoods</u></a>. It also starts and ends Downtown, which is more convenient than races where participants are transported 26 miles away and wait hours for the race to start, often before dawn.</p><p>And because it’s a flat course, the Chicago Marathon is known as a fast race. It’s a prime choice to reach personal records or try to qualify for the elite Boston Marathon, the country’s oldest marathon.</p><p>For the 2027 Boston Marathon, the top five most popular qualifying races were the 2026 Boston Marathon (4,448 entrants), followed by last year’s Chicago Marathon (2,043 entrants), the New York City Marathon (826 entrants), the California International Marathon (812 entrants) and the 2026 London Marathon (610 entrants), according to the <a class="Link" href="https://www.baa.org/news/record-field-of-qualifiers-accepted-into-the-131st-boston-marathon-presented-by-bank-of-america/" target="_blank" ><u>Boston Athletic Association</u></a>.</p><h3>What else is distinctive about the Chicago Marathon?</h3><p>It is one of eight Abbott World <a class="Link" href="https://www.worldmarathonmajors.com/six-star/majors" target="_blank" ><u>Marathon Majors</u></a> — some of the largest and most renowned marathons globally. They include Tokyo, Boston, London, Cape Town, Sydney, Berlin, New York City and Chicago.</p><p>Participants who run one of the <a class="Link" href="https://www.worldmarathonmajors.com/rankings/how-it-works" target="_blank" ><u>eight races</u></a> are eligible for a global ranking in a championship marathon, held in Tokyo in 2027. Runners who compete in any of more than 375 qualifying marathons worldwide (including the Majors) can also qualify for the championship race.</p><h3>Where do Chicago Marathon participants come from?</h3><p>This year, more than 75% of participants will travel from outside of Illinois. They hail from all 50 states and more than 130 countries. The top source countries outside the U.S. are the United Kingdom, Mexico, Canada and Brazil.</p><p>The U.S. states with the most participants are Illinois, New York, California, Massachusetts and Texas. The top cities are Chicago, New York, London and Boston.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" Marathon.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Candace Dane Chambers/Sun-Times file</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p></p><h3>What’s the economic impact of the Chicago Marathon?</h3><p>In terms of tourism, the Chicago Marathon is a major economic driver for the city. In 2025, the Chicago Marathon injected nearly<a class="Link" href="https://newsroom.bankofamerica.com/content/newsroom/press-releases/2026/08/largest-bank-of-america-chicago-marathon-field-yet-fueled-by-ins.html" target="_blank" ><u> $756 million</u></a> into the Chicago area’s economy, representing a 7.5% increase over the 2024 race, according to an <a class="Link" href="https://newsroom.bankofamerica.com/content/dam/newsroom/docs/2026/031226_WAGNER_2025%20BACM%20Econ%20Imp%20Infographic.pdf" target="_blank" ><u>economic impact study</u></a>.</p><p>Many residents and business owners consider the marathon less of an inconvenience than other big events that create more traffic disruptions, noise and safety issues like the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/money/2025/07/03/chicago-businesses-nascar-economic-impact" target="_blank" >NASCAR </a>Chicago Street Race or the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2024-democratic-national-convention" target="_blank" ><u>Democratic National Convention</u></a>. </p><p>The marathon is an economic boost for Downtown Chicago, which like many city centers across the U.S. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/money/2026/07/21/loops-arts-and-culture-visitors-contribute-395-million-to-the-economy " target="_blank" >hasn’t recovered</a> fully from the COVID-19 pandemic.</p><p>“Marathon weekend is one of the most important dates on the calendar in Chicago,” Rich Gamble, then-interim CEO of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/money/2024/10/10/chicago-marathon-give-city-hefty-economic-boost-record-number-runners-tourists" target="_blank" ><u>Choose Chicago</u></a>, said in 2024.</p><p>This year, more than 20,000 international participants are expected.</p><p>In 2024, 35% of Chicago Marathon participants were international. “This is hugely beneficial for our local tourism and hospitality industry as <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/money/2024/10/10/chicago-marathon-give-city-hefty-economic-boost-record-number-runners-tourists" target="_blank" ><u>overseas tourists</u></a> tend to stay twice as long and spend twice as much as domestic visitors,” a Choose Chicago spokesperson said.</p><p>Whether big-name events really benefit greater Chicago or line organizers’ pockets is also a common debate. However, the Chicago Marathon <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/money/2024/10/10/chicago-marathon-give-city-hefty-economic-boost-record-number-runners-tourists " target="_blank" ><b>boosts business</b></a> in many neighborhoods along its route where spectators turn out.</p><h3>What’s the history of the Chicago Marathon?</h3><p>The first race was held Sept. 25, 1977. More than 4,200 runners gathered at Daley Plaza for the Mayor Daley Marathon, making it the largest marathon in the world at the time in terms of registered runners. However, just 2,128 finished the race.</p><p>As Chicago’s first marathon kicked off, the ceremonial starter’s cannon misfired into the crowd, injuring two spectators. "Ironically, the two burned were the wife and daughter of Wayne Goeldner, an original race founder," according to <a class="Link" href="https://cdn.chicagomarathon.com/app/uploads/2026/10/01130612/26-BACM-MEDIA-GUIDE-Race-History.pdf" target="_blank" ><u>race organizers</u></a>. "Despite the accident, the event ran very smoothly and, as advertised, was an event for the whole city to enjoy."</p><h3>How much do Chicago Marathon participants raise for charity?</h3><p>In 2025, athletes raising money for the marathon's official charity program raised a record <a class="Link" href="https://newsroom.bankofamerica.com/content/newsroom/press-releases/2025/12/bank-of-america-chicago-marathon-shatters-another-record---47-1-.html" target="_blank" ><u>$47.1 million for local, national and global nonprofits</u></a>. This year, about one-third of participants are expected to fundraise for charity.</p><p>Last year, Jim Preschlack of Lake Forest became the top fundraiser in the Chicago Marathon’s history. He raised $335,665 for lung cancer research at Northwestern University in honor of his wife, Paula, who was diagnosed with lung cancer last year.</p><h3>Who are the elite runners in the Chicago Marathon this year?</h3><p>2025 Chicago Marathon <a class="Link" href="https://newsroom.bankofamerica.com/content/newsroom/press-releases/2026/07/defending-champions-ready-to-take-on-stacked-field-at-48th-bank-.html" target="_blank" ><u>winners</u></a> Jacob Kiplimo of Uganda and Hawi Feysa of Ethiopia will return for this year’s race. Kiplimo <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-marathon/2025/10/12/jacob-kiplimo-wins-2025-chicago-marathon-conner-mantz-breaks-american-record" target="_blank" ><u>won last year’s Chicago Marathon</u></a> in the men’s division with a time of 2:02:23. In the women’s division, Feysa won with a time of 2:14:56, a personal best.</p><p>Conner Mantz shattered a long-standing American record with a time of 2:04:43.</p><p>Other professional athletes in this year’s marathon include Sharon Lokedi, Brigid Kosgei, Amos Kipruto and American Charles Hicks.</p><h3>What are course records for the Chicago Marathon?</h3><p>In 2023, Kelvin Kiptum of Kenya finished in 2:00:35 in the men’s division.</p><p>In 2024, Ruth Chepngetich of Kenya finished in 2:09:56 in the women’s division, according to <a class="Link" href="https://cdn.chicagomarathon.com/app/uploads/2026/10/01130612/26-BACM-MEDIA-GUIDE-Race-History.pdf" target="_blank" ><u>race organizers</u></a>.</p>

entries.title: Connor Bedard injury update: Inching toward return after three non-contact practices
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> will be a different team once Connor Bedard reenters their lineup.</p><p>For as flawed as they've looked during large portions of their first four games, it's worth noting their holes are widened and accentuated by the absence of their best player.</p><p>It goes beyond Bedard's own elite skills. When he's on the ice, he attracts the focus of defenses, opening more space for his linemates. When he's sidelined, the Hawks not only lack that but also have to move every other forward one slot higher on the depth chart than they're supposed to be.</p><p>Bedard has unfortunately missed a number of games already in his young career — 31 and counting — and most of those have gone poorly for the Hawks. It's harder to keep that context in mind, though, when those games come at the start of a new season, as these are.</p><p>It was interesting how woeful the Sharks looked Monday against the Stars — mustering only 13 shots on goal in a 5-0 loss — during Macklin Celebrini's first game missed since November 2024. The Hawks have encountered that situation much more frequently than their rebuilding counterpart to the west.</p><p>For the first time in Bedard's career, however, the Hawks have assembled a decent collection of forward talent beyond him. Once they can slot him alongside Patrick Kane, Frank Nazar, Tyler Bertuzzi, Anton Frondell and Roman Kantserov, they'll have a somewhat legitimate top six at long last.</p><p>And it might not be too long until that day comes.</p><p>Bedard, who on Thursday will be exactly three months removed from <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/07/08/blackhawks-connor-bedard-shoulder-surgery-injury-timeline" >left shoulder surgery</a>, has now been a partial participant in three consecutive practices, albeit in a non-contact jersey.</p><p>On Wednesday, he maneuvered around Nick Lardis, Kevin Korchinski and Ethan Del Mastro in one slightly closer-quarters drill than the full-rink "flow" drills he did Monday and Tuesday.</p><p>"It's obviously a process, but it's nice when you can start doing your normal things and get back on the ice," Bedard said Tuesday on Chicago Sports Network. And as a friend, it's fun to have him back on the ice."</p><p>The Hawks haven't shared when Bedard will undergo a doctor's exam that could clear him for contact, which would allow him to fully participate in practices and — probably not long after — make his season debut. </p><p>But it certainly seems possible that could happen by the end of October.</p><p>"It looks like's skating well, moving well and shooting well — all the stuff with the upper body," Kane said. entries.title: Block 37 sold to Orland Park real estate firm that plans mall rebrand — and a new name
entries.summary: <p>Orland Park-based Edwards Realty Co. announced Wednesday that it purchased Block 37 for $30 million, with plans to revamp the consumer experience at the Loop shopping mall.</p><p>The firm said it will focus on diversifying the mall's tenants through a mix of retail, entertainment and new restaurants. There's also plans to change the storied mall's name, as rebranding and modernization efforts take place.</p><p>“I view success as us adding value to the community that we're in by providing shopping, dining, service uses [and] entertainment experiences,” Ramzi Hassan, president of Edwards Realty Co., said. “It's as simple as leaving it better than we got it. This is a very important acquisition for our company, and all our attention is on it.”</p><p>Edwards Realty closed on the sale Tuesday with Chicago-based Republic Bank, financial partner LFI Energy and The Rose Family Office. </p><p>The seller, Los Angeles-based <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2012/4/10/18534110/la-based-firm-acquires-block-37-retail-complex-in-loop" >CIM Group</a>, purchased Block 37 at 108 N. State St. in 2012 from Bank of America, which foreclosed on the property in 2011 after its developer, Joseph Freed and Associates, defaulted on a debt estimated at $206 million. At the time, the five-story, 275,000-square-foot complex was only about 30% occupied.</p><p>CIM Group didn't respond to a request for comment.</p><p>Edwards Realty has a track record of turning around struggling shopping centers, including those in the Chicago suburbs. The firm, alongside Core Acquisitions, purchased Burr Ridge Village Center in 2019. The 200,000-square-foot property was 60% leased when the firms acquired it. After renovations and adding new tenants, the center's occupancy increased to more than 95%.</p><p>Edwards Realty also owns the shopping centers Orland Park Crossing and The Boulevard in St. Louis, along with a variety of strip malls in the Chicago suburbs.</p><p>Block 37 is the company's first acquisition in Downtown Chicago.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-630000" name="image-630000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b63068f/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6925x3886+0+53/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F99%2Fee%2F9fb4c7424fd69c4daa2eceda4f5c%2Fblock37-261008-3.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/dd7ccbc/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6925x3886+0+53/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F99%2Fee%2F9fb4c7424fd69c4daa2eceda4f5c%2Fblock37-261008-3.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b3a7980/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6925x3886+0+53/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F99%2Fee%2F9fb4c7424fd69c4daa2eceda4f5c%2Fblock37-261008-3.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Pedestrian walks by the entrance of Block 37 at 108 N. State St. in the Loop." srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b3a7980/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6925x3886+0+53/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F99%2Fee%2F9fb4c7424fd69c4daa2eceda4f5c%2Fblock37-261008-3.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/afd1e72/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6925x3886+0+53/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F99%2Fee%2F9fb4c7424fd69c4daa2eceda4f5c%2Fblock37-261008-3.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/b3a7980/2147483647/strip/true/crop/6925x3886+0+53/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F99%2Fee%2F9fb4c7424fd69c4daa2eceda4f5c%2Fblock37-261008-3.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Block 37 at 108 N. State St. in the Loop</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Pat Nabong/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>“We've been looking [in Downtown Chicago] for quite some time,” Hassan said. “Besides the incredible location, the history of [Block 37] is pretty checkered, with trying to get this development off the ground, then it finally coming to fruition and it having struggles. That fits what we do … because we are distressed asset investors that are primarily invested in retail.”</p><p>Hassan sees Block 37 as a big opportunity for the family-owned and -operated firm, despite the building’s history of struggling to secure retail and entertainment tenants. </p><p>He said the mall is currently about 65% leased. Tenants include AMC Theatres, Zara, Sephora, Akira, Gayle's Best Ever Grilled Cheese and Five Iron Golf.</p><p>It plans to add national, regional and local stores. Hassan said malls of the past fell into the habit of relying on big-name national brands to fill their space and drive sales. But now, where so much of shopping is done online, consumers want to visit malls for unique experiences and concepts they can’t find elsewhere. </p><p>Edwards Realty has partnered with local entrepreneurs at some of the firm’s other properties to help get them into a storefront. Hassan plans a similar “incubator” space for small businesses at Block 37. Also planned are brand activations, live performances and other programming in some of the common spaces. </p><p>As for the building itself, he said it’s in great shape. Work will mostly include modernization and rebranding efforts, such as a new color palette and signage. He expects the rebrand to be complete in six months. Shoppers could notice changes as early as Jan. 1, 2027. </p><p>Hassan said some new leases are already being finalized, and other “exciting and non-traditional” changes will be announced in the future.</p><p>Retailers, including shopping malls, have struggled to regain their footing after the COVID-19 pandemic kept shoppers home. But Hassan has faith that Chicago’s retail is seeing a rebound. He’s encouraged by the uptick in leasing along Michigan Avenue and believes State Street isn’t far behind.</p><p>Colliers data from August puts the retail vacancy rate in Chicago at 7.7%. That’s up slightly from the 7.4% vacancy rate reported at the end of 2025 — but the commercial real estate firm predicts vacancy will drop by the end of 2026.</p><p>“We have a huge customer base that we can satisfy and serve that have not been served yet, and we're prepared to make the investments to do those things,” Hassan said. “But the synergies have to be right. They have to be complementary uses, businesses, tenants. That's what we really focus on.”</p>
